articles.description:
What is DIP?


Dependency Inversion Principle is one of the SOLID Principle.

It states that High Level Module shouldn't depend on low level modules, Both should depend on abstraction.
Means, the code that handles business-logic shouldn't depend directly on the implementation details. Instead they both should depend on interfaces/abstract Class.
Suppose we have to 2 Modules,Car Module and Engine Module and Car Module uses Engine Module. Now if we are using DIP then we can swap Diesal Engine to Petrol Engine. Otherwise I have to make changes in the Car Module also.
We can do this using either interface injection or abstract class injection.
NestJS we attach a token to the Service we want to inject in the service.
interface IPlanService {
  canReview(): boolean;
}

export PlanService impleme…
articles.title: Scale APP using Dependency Inversion Principle

articles.author: Yannis
articles.description:
In this short tutorial you will create a serverless application that can receive requests and send responses back using Transmitters (TX) instead of APIs. 
Resources


Neuronum Lib: https://pypi.org/project/neuronum/5.3.0/
Installation





pip install neuronum          # install Neuronum dependencies

Create Account





neuronum create-cell          # create Neuronum Cell

Delete your account with: neuronum delete-cell
Setup Your App





neuronum init-node --app      # initialize a Node with app template

Change into Node Folder
cd node_                      # change directory

Start Node:
neuronum start-node           # start Node

Send A Request To Your App



Connect To Neuronum: https://neuronum.net/connect

Open your Transmitter (TX): https://neuronum.net/explore (you can find your TX ID in the app.py file of your Node Folder)
Activate your Transmitter
articles.title: Transmitters (TX): The Next API Killer? [Dev Tutorial]

articles.author: Maureen Mukami
articles.description:
Power BI is a powerful tool for data analysis and visualization, but its real strength lies in how it connects different tables through relationships. These relationships allow you to combine data, filter across tables, and create interactive reports with ease.
📘 What Are Relationships
🧩 How Relationships Are Categorized
Cardinality


Cross-filter direction



1️⃣ Cardinality
a. One to Many (1:*)
b. Many to One (*:1)
c. One to One (1:1)
d. Many to Many (:)
2️⃣ Cross-filter Direction
a. Single Direction
As I conclude, I’d like to emphasize that defining relationships correctly in Power BI is critical to building a robust and accurate data model. By understanding cardinality and cross-filter direction, you can ensure your data behaves as expected across dashboards and reports. Take the time to plan your relationships carefully they are the backbone of meaningful, interactive insights in Power BI.
articles.title: Relationships in Power BI
